newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BLEARY-EYED WOMEN GET CHAMPIONMSHIPS UNDERWAY.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BLEARY-EYED WOMEN GET CHAMPIONMSHIPS UNDERWAY.

text.p: Helena Fuchsova of the Czech Republic set the fastest time in the opening round of the women's 400 metres on Saturday as the sixth world championships got underway just 90 minutes after sunrise.
"Obviously this time of the day agree with me because that's the fastest time I've ever run," said the world indoor bronze medallist.
"It was scary, when we arrived here this morning, the stadium was still in darkness," said American Kim Graham, who won the third heat at 8.26 a.m. in 51.92 seconds.
Sandie Richards of Jamaica, the winner of the second heat in 51.57 seconds, added: "I have been up since five o'clock and I am still sleepy. It's kind of cruel but we have to do it."

Australian Cathy Freeman, the Olympic silver medallist and the fastest woman in the world this year and one of the favourites for the gold, had a little more time to wake up as her race did not start until 8.42 a.m..

She finished second to Jamaican Lorraine Graham in the final heat and said: "My eyes were still blurry. It's not natural to run at this time of the day. I have been up since five and still feel half asleep."
Graham won the heat in 51.45 seconds while Freeman clocked 51.53.
There were no surprises with American Jearl Miles-Clark, the 1993 world champion and another title contender, coming through in 51.77 seconds.
German Grit Breuer (51.43), silver medallist in 1991 and Pauline Davis of the Bahamas (51.61), the silver medallist two years ago, also qualified with ease.
